text:
noah: hi everyone, first-day kubectl puzzler. I followed the onboarding guide (aws sso + eks update-kubeconfig) but `kubectl get pods -n noah-dev` gives `Error: exec plugin: invalid apiVersion "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1"` and then Forbidden. any clues?

ingrid: hey noah, welcome! that error usually means your kubeconfig has an old exec plugin block (v1alpha1) that new kubectl treats as incompatible. What kubectl version are you on? (`kubectl version --client --short`)

noah: client v1.27.2 on macOS 13, installed via brew. the kubeconfig `users:` exec block is from `aws eks update-kubeconfig` though.

kai: fwiw AWS CLI v2 sometimes writes `apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1` depending on eksctl/aws-iam-authenticator versions. Two options: (1) upgrade aws-cli/eks plugin so it writes v1beta1, or (2) edit `~/.kube/config` and change `apiVersion` to `client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1` for the exec user entry.

noah: if I change the apiVersion manually will that break anything later when I re-run update-kubeconfig?

ingrid: it's fine as a short-term fix, but prefer upgrading the aws cli: `brew upgrade awscli` or reinstall via AWS installer so `eks update-kubeconfig` emits v1beta1. Also check `which aws` to ensure PATH isn't picking an old pip install.

noah: updated aws cli, re-ran `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` then `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-onboard`. kubeconfig now has `client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1`. kubectl still shows Forbidden on `kubectl get pods -n noah-dev`.

kai: that Forbidden is RBAC. Run `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n noah-dev` to confirm. New hires are usually granted a namespaced rolebinding called `onboard-edit` or `dev-edit`. File the access form if you haven't.

noah: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n noah-dev` -> no. I submitted the access form but not sure the exact namespace name to request.

ingrid: use `noah-dev` as the namespace (we create it on first request). In the form pick "Kubernetes namespace access" and request role `onboard-edit`. If you need a faster workaround we can issue a temporary serviceaccount kubeconfig for the ticket.

infra-bot: access request created by noah at 2018000012  id K-44590. Assigned to infra oncall. ETA: ~1h.

noah: quick follow-up for others who hit this: macOS + homebrew aws-cli sometimes leaves an old `aws-iam-authenticator` binary around. I had to remove `/usr/local/bin/aws-iam-authenticator` and `brew link awscli` so the new aws cli's eks plugin is used. Leaving the tiny command I used: `rm /usr/local/bin/aws-iam-authenticator && brew reinstall awscli`

kai: nice troubleshooting tip. also remember to `aws sso login` again after infra approves so the SSO session picks up the role mapping. :thumbsup:

noah: infra approved, re-ran `aws sso login`, `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n noah-dev` -> yes, and `kubectl get pods -n noah-dev` shows the pods. thanks all!
